Noah: Quick heads-up: onboarding Seren-7B (HF checkpoint -> redwood) for int8 perf run. Baseline fp16 looks good but our int8 convert shows accuracy skew concentrated on quotes and parentheses tokens.
Noah: Convert used: `python tools/hf_to_rd.py --hf-model seren/seren-7b --out rd/seren-7b --quant int8`
Sana: Do we know if HF used fused qkv or split q/k/v? That usually explains head-focused divergence. Also which tokenizer normalizer was used upstream?
Noah: HF archive had `qkv.weight` fused. Our converter split it into three by slicing contiguous ranges. Per-head similarity vs fp16 drops around heads 5-11.
Diego: Could be interleaved qkv layout. Another angle: check rotary config. Some Mobius-derived models use headwise rotary scaling which our export currently flattens to global scale. Quant makes that worse.
Lea: Also check vocab mapping: we previously saw that curly quotes and narrow no-break space map differences cause punctuation errors. Did you compare token id lists for first 5k tokens?
Noah: Ran a quick compare: 0.03% id mismatches around punctuation and ligatures. I suspect upstream uses NFKC normalization; our pipeline defaulted to NFC.
Sana: Two quick experiments: 1) re-run conversion with `--qkv-mode=interleaved` (if available) or add a reorder script; 2) force pre-tokenize NFKC normalize and re-tokenize. That will narrow root cause.
Noah: I added a local `--qkv-reorder=interleave` patch and re-converted. Int8 dev-suite error rate dropped from 7.8% to 1.2% on the chat-summarize set. Looks like qkv ordering was majority cause.
Diego: Good. For the remaining 1.2% we should instrument per-head rotary phase mismatch test: feed a repeating token sequence and plot phase drift across positions. If headwise scale differs, we'll see diverging phase offsets.
Lea: I'll run a tokenizer sweep over 200k tokens. If NFKC fixes the punctuation mismatch we can add a normalizer shim to converter. Also propose adding a small token-id parity check in conversion CI (map first 3k ids and fail if any mismatch).
Noah: Plan: (a) make converter try both split modes and choose the one with higher median per-head cosine to fp16 sample, (b) emit `qkv_layout` metadata in manifest, (c) include tokenizer-normalizer hint in manifest.
Sana: On runtime: make KV cache include `layout` tag so warm-starting caches can be permuted on load. That avoids cross-version rollouts failing silently.
Diego: I'll add a microbenchmark that warm-starts a quant model with fp16 cache and asserts next-token logits within epsilon after permute. Add it to eng-ml CI.
ci-bot: CI kicked off: `eng-ml/seren-convert-matrix` (variants: split-detect, rotary-scan, tokenizer-check) -> https://ci.redwood/internal/13579
Noah: CI quick result: detect-reorder picked `interleaved`. Rotary scan shows slight headwise amplitude variance but within tolerances. Tokenizer-check flagged NFC->NFKC diffs and recommends shim. Artifacts uploaded.
Lea: Action items: Noah -> PR to add auto-detect reorder + manifest fields + README note. Sana -> runtime KV layout tag + permute shim. Diego -> add warm-start microbench to CI. Lea -> normalizer shim + token-id parity test.
Noah: Adding note to onboarding doc: "When converting HF fused-qkv checkpoints, run auto-detect reorder and token-id parity check before tagging model as ready for canary". :thumbsup: 
ci-bot: CI finished: matrix succeeded, 1 advisory (rotary head variance) -> https://ci.redwood/internal/13579/artifacts
Sana: Thanks team. We'll run gated canary on Dedicated tomorrow and monitor summarize SLOs closely. If anyone reproduces punct-sensitive PPL jumps, follow the checklist and ping eng-ml.
